history.meta_title: Our Story — La Casa de los Juegos
history.meta_description: Since 1892 in Granada, guardians of board games, puzzles and playful curiosities from around the world. Discover the story of the Valdivia family.
history.intro_1: In the heart of Granada's Alcaicería, where the scent of sandalwood and spices still dances in the fresh air, a sanctuary for intellect and leisure was born over a century ago.
history.intro_2: La Casa de los Juegos was not conceived merely as a shop, but as a bridge between civilizations, carved in walnut wood and marked by the passage of time. Every board, every piece, every card that crossed our threshold was treated as a sacred artifact.
history.intro_3: For three generations, the Valdivia family guarded the secrets of ancient games. From Egyptian Senet to the intricate puzzles of the Qing dynasty, the workshop in the back room witnessed the constant creak of gouges and the meticulous polishing of bone dice.
history.blockquote: Play is the highest form of research
history.blockquote_cite: Frequently quoted by our founder, Don Aurelio Valdivia
history.section2_p1: After fifty years of uninterrupted service, Don Aurelio Valdivia III decided that his wise but tired hands needed rest. The closure of the physical shop in 2023 marked the end of an era for Granada, but not for the spirit of the brand.
history.section2_p2a: "A game doesn't end when the box is closed"
history.section2_p2c: "it is only saved for the next session"
history.section2_p2_full: "A game doesn't end when the box is closed", he always said, "it's just saved for the next session".
history.section2_p3: The transition to the digital world was our most challenging move. We weren't looking to become a faceless corporation, but rather a
history.section2_p5: Every pixel of this new home has been designed with the same reverence with which Aurelio carved a boxwood bishop.
history.photo2_caption: Don Aurelio on his last day in the workshop, 2023
history.final_p: Every game you find in our shop carries over a century of passion, tradition and artisanal dedication. Be part of this story.

timeline.card_1_description: Don Aurelio Valdivia founds the first Casa de los Juegos in the Alcaicería of Granada. A small workshop that combined toy repair and the sale of handcrafted games.
timeline.card_2_description: The Valdivia family expands the business and incorporates a carpentry workshop specializing in chess boards and hand-carved pieces.
timeline.card_3_description: Fernando Valdivia takes the reins of the family business and begins importing board games from all over Europe and Asia, making the store a cultural reference.
timeline.card_4_description: Opening of the emblematic location on Calle Recogidas. It becomes a meeting point for chess players, collectors and game lovers.
timeline.card_5_description: Casa de los Juegos receives Granada’s Gold Medal for its contribution to the city’s playful culture for over a century.
timeline.card_6_description: Don Aurelio Valdivia III retires after 50 years of service. The physical shop closes but the legacy continues.
timeline.card_7_description: Casa de los Juegos opens its doors in the digital world, bringing the magic of Granada to homes across Spain.
